## CLIENT SUCCESS STORY: ATTAINING A $962,500 SETTLEMENT FOR A NECK INJURY ARISING FROM A COMMERCIAL TRUCK COLLISION
A truck driver was headed west on US 287. However, they failed to pay attention and made an unsafe lane change while driving. A motorist was hit, and she suffered a neck injury. She also had a previous major spine surgery in her medical history.
Pre-existing conditions, unfortunately, can be used by insurance companies to minimize what they must pay out. We anticipated they would argue that at least some of the driver’s injuries were due to her prior major spine surgery.
While it may be the case that a prior surgery could impact current injuries, Texas law uses a standard known as “[The Eggshell Doctrine](https://www.mullenandmullen.com/personal-injury-lawyer/articles/how-the-eggshell-skull-helps-win-fair-compensation/).” This means you must take the plaintiff as you find them, which means they should be compensated for all injuries due to this accident (even if pre-existing conditions exacerbate those injuries).
To help the client win her claim, Shane Mullen recommended all new and increased symptoms be properly documented. This meant the client should get medical documentation of any new symptoms she noticed after the accident. The client underwent multiple laminectomies to remove damaged vertebrae.
When negotiations with the insurer began, they predictably argued the force of the accident could not have resulted in the need for surgery. So, Shane drew attention to the documented new symptoms, and the fact that even a moderate accident could aggravate pre-existing injuries.
**Ultimately, the insurer was forced to pay $962,500.00. And the client saved $70,000 with our reduced 29% case fee because her claim was settled out of court!**

Practically understanding a situation and legally proving liability are two different things. Fortunately, civil cases require a lower burden of proof than criminal ones. In civil cases, you simply need a “preponderance of the evidence” to win. This means there’s a greater than 50% chance that your claim is true.
To prove your claim’s truth, our lawyers look for the following:
### Were You Owed A Duty Of Care?
First, you must have some sort of legal or formal relationship with the defendant. For example, if this is another driver, they have a duty to obey the law, focus on driving, and pay attention to other motorists. However, if you get hurt while trespassing on someone else’s property, they likely don’t owe you a duty of care. And most likely you won’t be able to recover compensation for your injuries.
### Was Your Duty Of Care Breached?
Personal injury law allows people to make mistakes. However, they generally must exercise the same amount of care a reasonable person would in those circumstances. If they don’t, you can likely hold the defendant legally liable for their actions. So, to be a victim of medical malpractice, you must show the doctor caused you harm in a way that a reasonable doctor in the same situation would not have. Doctors can still make mistakes.
### Did You Experience Damages As A Result Of The Breach?
Your damages may seem to have obviously happened because of another party’s negligence. However, legally proving someone else caused those injuries can be quite difficult. Medical malpractice is the hardest type of personal injury claim to prove. It usually requires many witnesses to show a medical professional acted negligently.
### Did The Damages Or Injury Happen Within The Last 2 Years?
Texas has a 2-year statute of limitations for all personal injury claims (with a few rare exceptions). If you wait longer than this two-year timeline, your claim will be thrown out of court. While two years seems like a long time, you’re wise to file your claim as soon after your accident as you can. This gives your personal injury lawyer the most time possible to manage your claim. However, you only must file your claim within the two-year time limit. You do not have to go through court within that time limit (in the rare cases when it’s necessary).
### Don’t Make Crucial Mistakes
You don’t have to be completely perfect to win your claim. However, you can make mistakes that could dramatically reduce what you can recover, or that could even cost you your claim entirely. For example, giving the insurer too much information could potentially cause either of those outcomes. Remember that no matter how much the insurer seems to be on your side, they will use whatever you say against you to the greatest extent possible. And this includes your own insurance company. This is another reason why it’s wise to contact a personal injury lawyer in Frisco as soon after your injury as possible. One can advise you on how to avoid such mistakes.
